subject: general
question:
What is the median of the following distribution?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/732d69437c0dd90b2d9592fdbc81edd9319eceb2bf3091df292e237d394caeae.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Calculate **Cumulative Frequency (cf)**: 10, 22, 40, 60, 80.

Total frequency **N = 80**, so **N/2 = 40**.

Since the **cumulative frequency** of the class 200−220 is exactly 40 (N/2), the **Median** is the upper limit of this class.

**∴ The correct answer is 220.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Data:**

Class Intervals: 160−180, 180−200, 200−220, 220−240, 240−260

Frequencies (f): 10, 12, 18, 20, 20

**Formula Used:**

Median = L + [(N/2 − cfₚ) / fₘ] × h

Where **L** = Lower limit of median class, **N** = Total frequency, **cfₚ** = Cumulative frequency of preceding class, **fₘ** = Frequency of median class, **h** = Class width.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28a4c6026d0bb7d4860d491bcbf86e7e505648dde326810fa34af207f43cd7a5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cumulative Frequencies: 10, 22, 40, 60, 80

⇒ Total Frequency **N = 80**

⇒ **N/2 = 80 / 2 = 40**

⇒ The cumulative frequency just greater than or equal to 40 is 40, which belongs to class **200−220**.

⇒ L = 200, cfₚ = 22, fₘ = 18, h = 20

⇒ Median = 200 + [(40 − 22) / 18] × 20

⇒ Median = 200 + [18 / 18] × 20

⇒ Median = 200 + 20 = 220

**∴ The correct answer is 220.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Median for Grouped Data

Median is the value that divides the data into two equal halves. For grouped data, it is calculated using the interpolation formula based on the **Median Class**.

Mean of Grouped Data

Mean (μ) = Σ(fᵢ × xᵢ) / Σfᵢ, where xᵢ is the class mark (mid-point) of each interval.</p
